AutoVybz only calibrates loudspeakers. Disconnect headphones or headsets and connect a speaker.
The phone\'s own speaker can\'t be measured with its own microphone. Connect an external speaker via Bluetooth, cable, USB or HDMI.
The test plays noise and a sweep from deep bass (20 Hz) to very high tones (20 kHz) for 10 seconds. Media volume has been set to about 70 %.

No calibrations yet – start one in the wizard.
Connect the speaker you want to calibrate via Bluetooth, AUX cable, USB or HDMI and play something briefly to check it works. Headphones are blocked on purpose – AutoVybz is made for loudspeakers.

• Put the phone where you usually listen (sofa, desk chair) at about ear height.
• The main microphone is usually at the bottom edge – point it towards the speaker.
• Distance: 1–2 m for room speakers, 50–80 cm for small desktop speakers.
• Lay the phone on something soft or a stack of books, not directly on a table (reflections).
• Don't hold it in your hand – your body changes the sound.
AutoVybz sets the phone\'s media volume to about 70 %. Set the speaker itself to a normal, comfortable listening level. If the result says „overloaded“, turn down; if it says „quiet“, turn up.
Close windows, switch off fans or the dishwasher and don\'t talk during the 10 seconds. AutoVybz measures the background noise first and warns you if it was too loud.

Dolby Atmos, „Adapt Sound“, bass boost or the EQ in your speaker\'s app change what AutoVybz measures. Turn them off before measuring – you can switch them on again later. The AutoVybz EQ pauses itself automatically.

Bluetooth adds 100–300 ms delay. AutoVybz finds the exact delay itself, so you don\'t need to do anything. Many party speakers have built-in bass boost that changes with volume – calibrate at the volume you usually use.

The speaker plays pink noise and a logarithmic sine sweep (20 Hz – 20 kHz) for exactly 10 seconds while the phone records. AutoVybz calculates the frequency response, compensates the typical behaviour of phone microphones, smooths it (stronger in the bass, 1/3 octave in mids and highs) and fits up to 10 parametric filters that bring your speaker towards the chosen target. A negative pre-gain and the limiter prevent clipping.

Phone microphones are not measurement microphones; the built-in profiles are estimates. Deep bass the speaker physically can\'t play is never boosted (protects the speaker). For lab-grade results use a USB measurement microphone with its calibration file (Pro area).
AutoVybz is 100 % open source and donationware: no ads, no tracking, no paywall.

AutoVybz records 10 seconds of audio only during a measurement. Nothing leaves your phone.
One 10-second measurement at your listening spot.

Three 10-second measurements around your listening spot (about 30 s plus moving the phone). Averaging keeps the room booms everyone hears and ignores dips that only exist at one spot – recommended for rooms and bass.
Now move the phone about 30–50 cm – to the side, forward or back, or a little up or down.
Stay around your listening spot and keep the phone at ear height.
Microphone towards the speaker, hold still and stay quiet during the measurement.
Best repeat this measurement – or continue anyway.
The positions differ a lot. That is normal in very uneven rooms – otherwise stay closer to your listening spot or measure when it is quieter.
Happy with the sound? Show your friends – the share card shows your real measurement.

Living room, office, party basement – room resonances are corrected precisely.
Garden, terrace, beach, park: optimised for loudness (max. +3 dB boost), ignores ground reflections and noisy ranges, detects wind and Bluetooth dropouts, limiter always on. 3 positions recommended.
Turn the speaker up properly – as loud as for the party, but not to maximum.
Put the phone 2–4 m in front of the speaker at ear height (chair, table, backpack) – not on the ground.
Wind: turn the microphone opening (usually at the bottom) away from the wind; a thin cloth over it helps. Wait for a calm moment.
Wind, background noise and Bluetooth dropouts are detected automatically.
Now walk 1–2 m further: spread the positions over the area where people will dance and listen.
Same height (ear height), microphone towards the speaker – don\'t put the phone on the ground.
Strong low-frequency noise (wind on the microphone, traffic, generator). The affected range is not corrected. With wind: shield the microphone and measure again.
Background noise changed a lot (gusts, cars, voices). If the result looks odd, measure again at a quieter moment.
The signal dropped out briefly – typical for Bluetooth at the edge of its range. Move the phone closer to the speaker and measure again.
Not corrected because of background noise: %1$s
Pre-gain only %1$s dB: outdoors AutoVybz boosts by 3 dB at most and prefers cutting – so you keep the loudness for the party.
The limiter is switched on automatically when you activate this calibration and protects the speaker at party volume.
Party tip: extra bass comes free with placement – put the speaker on the ground (up to +6 dB) or close to a wall. Then measure again.
Outdoors a single position is unreliable (ground reflection). With 3 positions the result gets much more accurate.

Outdoors there are no walls – that changes the acoustics completely. Choose „Outdoors · Party“ in the wizard:
• Less bass: indoors the walls lift the bass by about 4–8 dB; outdoors that is missing. Making up for it with EQ costs exactly as much loudness and strains the woofer. That is why outdoor mode boosts by 3 dB at most and prefers cutting. Extra bass comes free with placement: speaker on the ground (up to +6 dB), close to a wall or a house corner (even more).
• Ground reflection: sound bouncing off the ground cancels single frequencies, depending on where you stand. No EQ can fill these holes – AutoVybz ignores them and averages 3 positions. Spread them 1–2 m apart over the area where people will be.
• Wind & noise: wind on the microphone causes strong bass rumble. Turn the microphone opening away from the wind, put a thin cloth over it and wait for a calm moment. Frequencies where wind, traffic, birds or cicadas are louder than the speaker are automatically left uncorrected – the result shows which ones.
• Distance & level: measure 2–4 m in front of the speaker, turned up properly (party level, but not maximum – many party speakers turn their bass down there).
• Bluetooth range: outdoors no walls reflect the signal. Keep the phone near the speaker; dropouts are detected.
• Two speakers / party mode: measure each speaker on its own or put them close together – two speakers far apart cause strong interference outdoors.
• Sun: in outdoor mode AutoVybz turns the screen brightness up during the calibration. The limiter is always switched on when activating.
